rows.name: open?

rows.name: presentation?
rows.notes: Defaults to `auto`, which the density resolves into `popup` or `sheet`.

rows.name: matchWidth?
rows.notes: `true` by default — the select's divergence from the menu (ROADMAP): a surface of options is a widened trigger, so its width is the anchor's.

rows.group: positioning, handed straight to the positioner

rows.name: getAnchorRect?
rows.notes: Anchor to a rect rather than an element — a caret, a canvas, a cell.
rows.group: positioning, handed straight to the positioner

rows.name: dir?
rows.notes: Not defaulted, deliberately: left unset the resolved page direction governs, so a subtree inside an RTL region inherits instead of being reset to `ltr`.

rows.name: closeOnSelect?
rows.notes: No per-item override, a deliberate divergence from the menu: a select that stays open after a choice is a setting of the surface, not of one item.

rows.name: highlightedValue?
rows.notes: The keyboard cursor, not the selection: arrows and typeahead move it, and `value` only follows once a choice is committed.

rows.name: closeOnEscape?
rows.notes: Governs the gamepad `back` intent as well: B and Escape share one lock.

rows.name: preventOutsideActivation?
rows.notes: The click that closes the select must not activate what was under it.

rows.name: modal?
rows.notes: `false` — the menu's justification, verbatim: inert + scroll lock is the dialog's contract.

rows.name: preventScroll?
rows.notes: Defaults to the `sheet` presentation and is ignored in `popup`.

rows.name: parentId?
rows.notes: The layer this select opened from — required once either end is portalled, or a click inside the portalled listbox reads as outside the surface that holds the trigger. Adapters default it from their layer context.

rows.name: restoreFocus?
rows.notes: On by default. Turned off, focus is left wherever the dismissal put it and `finalFocus` is never consulted.

rows.name: finalFocus?
rows.notes: Outranks the element that had focus when the select opened; ignored entirely while `restoreFocus` is off.

rows.name: selectionFlash?
rows.notes: The selection blink. Popup only; off in `sheet` and under reduced motion.

rows.name: label?
rows.notes: The accessible name of both halves when nothing else names them: the listbox stops borrowing the trigger's name, and the trigger — a `role="combobox"`, which takes no name from its contents — gets one at all. Inside a `field`, prefer the field's label; `labelledBy` outranks this.

rows.name: describedBy?
rows.notes: `aria-describedby` for the trigger — what a field's helper text wires in.

rows.name: labelledBy?
rows.notes: `aria-labelledby` for the trigger, for a label `label[for]` cannot reach.

rows.name: persistentElements?
rows.notes: Spared by both the outside-interaction test and the modal inert treatment — what must stay live under an open listbox.

rows.name: intents?
rows.notes: The intent bus engage mode pushes its scope onto. `null` by default, so the pad is off until a host is supplied.

rows.name: placeholder?
rows.notes: Shown by the trigger while nothing is selected.

rows.name: trigger?
rows.notes: Handed to `SelectTrigger` as `render` — never as its children. The trigger *is* a `<button>`, and a button inside a button is `nested-interactive`. The substitution brings the element **and its behaviour** with it — `ButtonRoot` infers `nativeButton` from what it actually renders — and the look follows the element too: `_select.scss:41` and `:84` are the library's only `select:trigger` rules and both stand behind `:not([data-part*=" "])`, so the pop-up form withholds itself the moment a second identity lands on the element. That is the composition point the sheet declares out loud (`_select.scss:29-32`, "the button's sheet owns the form"), not an accident of source order. The chevron cell is not gated and stays: `select:indicator` is a child, not the composed element.

rows.name: cancelLabel?
rows.notes: The sheet's Cancel card. The part withholds itself in `popup` on its own, and `null` withholds it here — an empty `<button>` would have no accessible name, and `getCancelTriggerProps` writes none.

rows.name: keepMounted?
rows.notes: `true` by default, as on `SelectRoot` — the collection is in the markup while closed.

rows.name: renderOption?
rows.notes: Replaces the CHILDREN of an item, never the item. `defaults` is the row the layer would have rendered — indicator, symbol, text — and it is handed over so that **decorating** is the cheapest thing to do, not because replacing is impossible. Rendering something else instead of `defaults` is the consumer's to do and costs them three things: the part that names the option (`SelectItemText`), the selection checkmark, and the leading column those two share. Decorate as a **sibling** of `defaults`, never by wrapping it in an element: an item's children are its grid cells (`_select.scss:382`, `grid-template-columns` on `select:item`), so a wrapper collapses all three into one and a node with no `grid-column` of its own lands in the leading track.

name: SelectOption
definition: Omit< CoreSelectItemProps, "value" | "label" > & ComposedDecoration<Meta> & { readonly value: V; readonly label: string; }

rows.name: itemGroup?
rows.notes: Applied to EVERY group — `id` and `label` are the entry's, one per group.

rows.name: item?
rows.notes: Applied to EVERY item, hence no `id` **and no IDREF**: one `id` repeated down a listbox is a broken IDREF per row, and one `aria-labelledby` repeated gives every option the same name — which `danglingIdRefs` cannot see, because the id it points at does resolve. `ref` goes for the same reason: a single ref held by N rows ends up holding the last one.

rows.name: placeholder?
rows.notes: Shown while nothing is selected. `children` wins, then the captured label.

rows.name: id
rows.notes: Ties the group to its label. Any stable string the consumer owns.

rows.name: label?
rows.notes: The group renders an `itemGroupLabel` part — wires `aria-labelledby`. Declared, never assumed: written blind, the attribute is a dead IDREF *and* no accessible name at once (same shape as `MenuItemGroupProps.label`).
